approach: Make `take_baseline` (run/checks.rs) ask for a CI result before it runs anything locally. It does this only for a non-nested job whose origin is on GitHub. It reuses the candidate path unchanged: `routing::route`, `routing::run_routed_with_record` and so `ci_result::resolve`. They are called with the base commit (`ctx.prediction`) as the SHA, the base's branch (`git.current_branch()`, the branch the job was dispatched from, mod.rs:975) in place of the job's CI branch, one read and no wait, and an `Exec` that refuses to run anything. `resolve` then yields a green record from CI, a red one, or nothing (its local fallback calls the refusing `Exec` and errors). Only a green record whose reused runs all passed makes a reused baseline: `Baseline.checks` become the reused `CheckRun`s (`reused: true`) and a new optional field `reused_from` holds the run address. Any other result (missing, unfinished, red, lookup error, checks not covering fmt/clippy/test, no branch) falls through to today's local `baseline_checks`, unchanged, and the job's output says why. To make the branch a parameter, `with_ci_source` (mod.rs:1318) is split into `with_ci_source_on(branch, ...)` plus a thin wrapper that keeps its current behavior. A repository with no GitHub origin does no lookup and prints no extra line. The lookup is keyed on the base SHA, because `resolve` compares `run.sha` with the SHA it was given (ci_result.rs:196) and no code indexes CI runs by governed-content fingerprint. The base is usually main's head, which main's push run in ci.yml (`push: branches: [main, ...]`) has tested. This is a deliberate narrowing of 'same fingerprint', put to the user in open_questions.

decisions.choice: Reuse `routing::run_routed_with_record` with a refusing `Exec` and a one-read `Wait`, instead of calling `ci_result::resolve` directly or writing a new lookup.
decisions.reason: It is the existing candidate path (`resolve` + `runs_from_record`), so it gives reused `CheckRun`s with the same notes and `reused: true`. It also gives the red-run log detail, and it needs no new CI-reading code. Criterion 5 asks for the existing `resolve` path.

rejected.option: A new baseline-specific CI lookup in ci_result.rs
rejected.why: Duplicates `resolve`; criterion 5 forbids a new lookup.

decisions.choice: Look the run up by the base SHA on the job's dispatch branch (`git.current_branch()`), with one read and no wait.
decisions.reason: `CiBranchSource::fetch` filters by `head_sha`, `event=push` and `branch` (gh/client.rs:964-974), and `resolve` insists `run.sha == sha`. The base is normally a commit on the default branch with a push run on it. Waiting for an unfinished main run would be new polling, which is out of scope, and would delay every job.

rejected.option: Match by governed-content fingerprint across other commits' runs, e.g. the landed candidate's athena/ci/<job> run
rejected.why: The candidate's SHA is not known from the base. No code lists runs by fingerprint; finding it would need the records branch and a new host query. The change would grow well past one run.

rejected.option: Walk base ancestors and compare `fingerprint()` for each
rejected.why: Ancestors almost never share governed content. It adds an ls-tree and classify call per commit for little gain.

decisions.choice: Add `reused_from: Option<String>` to `Baseline` with `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`, and keep the schema tag `athena.baseline/1`.
decisions.reason: Old files parse. Files written without reuse are byte-identical to before. `check_record_file`, the allow-list and the `AnyRecord::Baseline` arm need no change.

rejected.why: Needs a new tag and allow-list work, and old files would not parse unchanged.

rejected.option: Only mark the individual `CheckRun`s as reused
rejected.why: The brief wants the baseline itself marked reused.

decisions.choice: The reuse decision and its reason go on a `ci         baseline ...` output line. `Baseline.note` stays unset on a fallback.
decisions.reason: `Baseline::failed_before` ignores any baseline that has a note (records.rs:2629). A note on a local fallback would stop real pre-existing failures from being excused, which changes the verdict rules and is out of scope.

rejected.option: Set `Baseline.note` on a red or error lookup
rejected.why: Would disable pre-existing-failure marking for that job (see above).

decisions.choice: Print no new line when there is no GitHub origin and in nested runs.
decisions.reason: The existing test `a_fake_job_takes_its_baseline_before_the_producer...` asserts exactly 8 lines for an origin-less repository (tests.rs:472).

rejected.why: Breaks that test and adds noise where no lookup was possible.

On a green all-passed result it fills `checks` and `reused_from`; otherwise it runs `baseline_checks` as today. A small `Exec` implementation refuses to run checks.

steps: Read `Kind::parse` and `path_rule_applies` in routing.rs, `runs_from_record`, the `Exec` trait, and the case where `run_routed_with_record` gets a Blocked outcome (Fallback error). Pick the kind that applies no path skipping.

records.rs: add `reused_from: Option<String>` to `Baseline` with `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` and a doc comment. Fix the `sample_baseline` literal, and extend the round-trip tests (with, without, and the old-form JSON).

checks.rs: add a private `RefuseExec` implementing `routing::Exec` (`exec` returns an error, `redact` passes text through). Add `reused_baseline(&self, ctx) -> Option<(Vec<CheckRun>, String)>`. It does nothing when `has_github_origin()` is false. Otherwise it takes `git.current_branch()` (no branch: print the reason and return None) and builds the route with an empty change list. If `!route.reuse` it prints the reason. It calls `run_routed_with_record(&route, &ctx.prediction, &[], ci, &RefuseExec, one_read)` inside `with_ci_source_on(branch, ..)`. It returns Some only for `Ok((runs, Some(record)))` with `record.source == Source::Ci`, `record.all_passed()` and all runs passed. Otherwise it prints `ci         baseline runs locally: <reason>`: red run with its address, or no usable CI result.

checks.rs `take_baseline`: after the nested early return, call `reused_baseline`. On Some, print `ci         baseline reused from <address> for <base>`, set `checks` and `reused_from = Some(address)`, and return without creating the snapshot. On None, continue with `baseline_checks` unchanged.

tests.rs: add `ci_reuse_run_with` (check command parameter; `ci_reuse_run` calls it with PASSES), `CiReply::Unreachable` (the runner returns Err, with arms added to `runs()` and `jobs()`), `baseline_reads()`, and narrow `reads()` to `branch=athena/ci/`. Write `baseline_reused_from_a_green_ci_run_runs_nothing_locally` and `baseline_runs_locally_when_no_green_ci_result_exists`, using `MARKS_BASELINE` and `<job_dir>/baseline-ran` for the local-run signal.

ci_result.rs: update the module doc only. Then run `cargo test -p athena-core`, `cargo test -p athena-data`, and the workspace `cargo test --locked`. Fix any integration or cli assertion changed by the green-for-everything GitHub fakes, naming each.

CHANGELOG.md: add the Unreleased entry (reuse from a green GitHub run for the base commit; otherwise a local run as before, with the reason on a `ci` line; local-baseline records unchanged). Finish with `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check`.

risks.risk: The base branch has no push run for the base SHA (a feature branch, detached HEAD, or main's run still running), so the saving does not appear.
risks.mitigation: This is the stated fallback: run locally as today and print the reason. No job fails because of the lookup. Detached HEAD gives a `no branch` reason.

risks.risk: Extra GitHub reads for every GitHub-origin job, and a read error breaking the baseline.
risks.mitigation: One read, no pause. `read_ci` already turns an error into Missing. Any Err from the routed call is caught and falls back to the local run.

risks.risk: `route(kind, ..)` with a kind that applies the path rule could skip checks. A reused baseline would then have fewer checks than a local one.
risks.mitigation: The producer reads `Kind::parse` and `path_rule_applies` and passes a kind with no path skipping, together with an empty change list. A test asserts the reused baseline has all three check names.

risks.risk: The integration fakes that answer every CI read green (test_support.rs:718) change what GitHub-origin integration jobs record as the baseline.
risks.mitigation: Run `cargo test --locked` for the workspace, adjust any affected assertion, and say so in the producer report.

risks.risk: Adding the field to `deny_unknown_fields` Baseline could make older Athena binaries refuse the newer file.
risks.mitigation: `skip_serializing_if` leaves local-baseline files unchanged. Only reused baselines carry the key, and the records are read by the same release.

demonstrations.method: New test `baseline_reused_from_a_green_ci_run_runs_nothing_locally` in run/tests.rs. It drives a whole job through `Athena::go`, as `ci_reuse_green_skips_local_checks` does. Its capability's check command is `MARKS_BASELINE` (`touch ../baseline-ran`, tests.rs:1907), which leaves a file in the job directory whenever the local baseline runs.
demonstrations.observes: Under CiReply::Green, the stored `Baseline` has `reused_from` set to the run address. Its checks are fmt, clippy and test with `reused` true and `passed` true. The file `<job_dir>/baseline-ran` does not exist, so `baseline_runs` never ran. The CI fake saw exactly one read on the base branch. Output contains `ci         baseline reused from <address> for <base sha>`.

demonstrations.seam: Production entry point is `Athena::go` (reaching `take_baseline` via `baseline_stage`). The fake is `ci_seam::install` with `CiReplies` (exists, tests.rs:2539, mod.rs:1216). It answers any `head_sha` and `branch`, so the base's lookup is answered too. The marker command is `MARKS_BASELINE` (exists). Step 7 adds `ci_reuse_run_with(origin, reply, check)`, which takes the check command, and `CiReplies::baseline_reads()`, which counts runs requests on the base branch. The guard is the GitHub origin: the fake origin is `GITHUB`, and the helper fails if the CI source was never read.

open_questions: User: The existing candidate reuse is keyed on the exact commit SHA (`resolve` requires `run.sha == sha`, ci_result.rs:196), not on the governed-content fingerprint, and no code indexes CI runs by fingerprint. This plan therefore looks up the base's own SHA on its branch, which covers main's push run of the base commit. It does not find the landed candidate's run on `athena/ci/<job>` when main's run is still unfinished. Is SHA-on-the-base-branch enough, or should a fingerprint-keyed lookup (which needs the records branch and a new host query) be a separate job?

Host: Does main's push run of ci.yml normally finish before the next job starts? The plan reads once with no wait, so a still-running main run means a local baseline. ci.yml triggers on push to main, but how often a run is already finished at dispatch time cannot be learned from the code.
